stops.name: The White House
stops.blurb: Home and office of the president since 1800.

stops.name: Capitol Rotunda
stops.blurb: Under the dome, where the nation honors its dead and its documents.

stops.name: Senate Chamber
stops.blurb: Two senators per state, treaties, nominations and trials.

stops.name: House Chamber
stops.blurb: Where bills must begin if they raise revenue.

stops.name: Supreme Court
stops.blurb: Equal justice under law, one landmark case at a time.

stops.name: Library of Congress
stops.blurb: The nation's library: maps, manuscripts, bills and ideas.

stops.name: National Archives
stops.blurb: Home of the Declaration, the Constitution and the Bill of Rights.

stops.name: Lincoln Memorial
stops.blurb: A marble temple for the Civil War president and for 1963.

stops.name: Washington Monument
stops.blurb: A 555-foot obelisk for the first president.

stops.name: Jefferson Memorial
stops.blurb: A domed rotunda on the Tidal Basin for the author of the Declaration.

stops.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial
stops.blurb: The Stone of Hope, beside the Tidal Basin.

stops.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt Memorial
stops.blurb: Four outdoor rooms for four terms, the Depression and the war.

stops.name: National WWII Memorial
stops.blurb: Fifty-six pillars and two arches for a world at war.

stops.name: Vietnam Veterans Memorial
stops.blurb: A black granite wall, cut into the earth, names in order of loss.

stops.name: Korean War Veterans Memorial
stops.blurb: Nineteen steel patrol figures moving through juniper.

stops.name: National Museum of American History
stops.blurb: From the Star-Spangled Banner to a lunch counter.

stops.name: African American History Museum
stops.blurb: A bronze-toned museum on the Mall telling the story of slavery, freedom and culture.

stops.name: National Museum of the American Indian
stops.blurb: A curving, sandstone-colored museum on the Mall's east end.

stops.name: National Air and Space Museum
stops.blurb: Wright Flyer, Spirit of St. Louis, Apollo 11.

stops.name: Ford's Theatre
stops.blurb: Where the Civil War presidency ended on April 14, 1865.

stops.name: Arlington National Cemetery
stops.blurb: Across the Memorial Bridge, on land that was once Lee's estate.

stops.name: The Pentagon
stops.blurb: Five sides, the Defense Department and the Cold War.

stops.name: U.S. Treasury
stops.blurb: Money, debt and Hamilton's financial system.

stops.name: Frederick Douglass House
stops.blurb: Cedar Hill, above Anacostia, home of the great abolitionist.

stops.name: Washington National Cathedral
stops.blurb: A Gothic landmark on the city's highest ground.

stops.name: Union Station
stops.blurb: Opened in 1907, a gateway for trains, workers and travelers.
